es.summary: El trastorno depresivo persistente es una forma crónica de depresión con síntomas leves a moderados que duran al menos dos años.
key_points: Duración mínima de 2 años con síntomas depresivos.
Menor intensidad que la depresión mayor, pero más prolongada.
Alteraciones en serotonina, norepinefrina y dopamina.
Riesgo de progresión a depresión mayor y suicidio.

pathophysiology: Disminución de serotonina, norepinefrina y dopamina en el cerebro.
Cambios estructurales en corteza prefrontal y amígdala.
Alteración de la neuroplasticidad y neurogénesis.
risk_factors: Historia familiar de trastornos del ánimo.
Aislamiento social y falta de apoyo.
signs_symptoms: Estado de ánimo deprimido la mayor parte del día.
Baja autoestima y sentimientos de inutilidad.
Cambios en el apetito o peso.
Dificultad para concentrarse y tomar decisiones.
diagnostics: Entrevista clínica con criterios DSM‑5: síntomas >2 años.
Escala PHQ‑9 o HAM‑D; puntuación ≥10 indica depresión.
Examen físico para descartar causas médicas.
Laboratorios básicos (TSH, glucosa, CBC) normalmente normales.
treatment: Apoyo psicosocial y grupos de auto‑ayuda.
complications: Disfunción ocupacional y deterioro de relaciones.
nursing_care: Evaluar estado de ánimo y nivel de ansiedad cada turno.
Monitorear adherencia a medicación y efectos secundarios.
Promover higiene del sueño y rutina diaria estructurada.
Fomentar actividad física ligera y exposición a luz natural.
Facilitar contacto con familia y redes de apoyo.
patient_teaching: Explicar la naturaleza crónica del TDP y la importancia del tratamiento continuo.
Enseñar técnicas de relajación (respiración diafragmática, mindfulness).
Instruir sobre reconocimiento de signos de empeoramiento y cuándo buscar ayuda.
Reforzar la toma regular de antidepresivos según indicación.
Promover hábitos de vida saludables (ejercicio, alimentación equilibrada).

outcomes: Ansiedad reducida: nivel ≤3/10 en escala de ansiedad
Participa en técnicas de relajación al menos 3 veces/semana

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de ansiedad usando escala de 0‑10 cada turno
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar cambios y responder oportunamente

interventions.action: Enseñar respiración diafragmática y práctica de mindfulness
interventions.rationale: Reduce la respuesta fisiológica al estrés

interventions.action: Proveer ambiente tranquilo, minimizar ruidos y estímulos excesivos
interventions.rationale: Facilita la autorregulación emocional

interventions.action: Facilitar expresión de sentimientos mediante conversación abierta
interventions.rationale: Ayuda a procesar emociones y disminuir la ansiedad

interventions.action: Colaborar con el médico para evaluar necesidad de ajuste farmacológico
interventions.rationale: Control farmacológico adecuado puede disminuir la ansiedad persistente

outcomes: Uso de al menos dos estrategias de afrontamiento efectivas
Mejora en puntuación de coping ≥4/10 en escala de afrontamiento

interventions.action: Identificar fuentes de estrés mediante entrevista estructurada
interventions.rationale: Permite focalizar intervenciones de afrontamiento

interventions.action: Enseñar habilidades de resolución de problemas paso a paso
interventions.rationale: Facilita la toma de decisiones y reduce la sensación de impotencia

interventions.action: Fomentar participación en grupos de apoyo o terapia grupal
interventions.rationale: Incrementa la red de apoyo y comparte estrategias efectivas

interventions.action: Derivar a trabajador social para recursos comunitarios y actividades recreativas
interventions.rationale: Amplía opciones de afrontamiento fuera del entorno hospitalario

interventions.action: Reforzar logros diarios y registrar avances en un diario de ánimo
interventions.rationale: Promueve la autoeficacia y la motivación

en.summary: Persistent Depressive Disorder is a chronic form of depression with mild to moderate symptoms lasting at least two years.
key_points: Minimum duration of 2 years with depressive symptoms.
Less intense than Major Depressive Disorder but more prolonged.
Alterations in serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine.
Risk of progression to Major Depressive Disorder and suicide.

pathophysiology: Reduced serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine in the brain.
Structural changes in prefrontal cortex and amygdala.
risk_factors: Social isolation and lack of support.
signs_symptoms: Depressed mood most of the day.
Low self‑esteem and feelings of worthlessness.
diagnostics: Clinical interview with DSM‑5 criteria: symptoms >2 years.
PHQ‑9 or HAM‑D scale; score ≥10 indicates depression.
Physical exam to rule out medical causes.
Basic labs (TSH, glucose, CBC) usually normal.
treatment: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) or Interpersonal Therapy.
complications: Increased risk of Major Depressive Disorder.
nursing_care: Assess mood and anxiety level each shift.
Monitor medication adherence and side effects.
Promote sleep hygiene and structured daily routine.
Encourage light physical activity and natural light exposure.
Facilitate contact with family and support networks.
patient_teaching: Explain the chronic nature of PDD and the importance of ongoing treatment.
Instruct on recognizing signs of worsening and when to seek help.
Reinforce regular antidepressant intake as prescribed.
Promote healthy lifestyle habits (exercise, balanced diet).

outcomes: Reduced anxiety: level ≤3/10 on anxiety scale
Participates in relaxation techniques at least 3 times/week

interventions.action: Assess anxiety level using 0‑10 scale each shift
interventions.rationale: Allows identification of changes and timely response

interventions.action: Teach diaphragmatic breathing and mindfulness practice
interventions.rationale: Reduces physiological response to stress

interventions.action: Provide a calm environment, minimize noise and excessive stimuli
interventions.rationale: Facilitates emotional self‑regulation

interventions.action: Facilitate expression of feelings through open conversation
interventions.rationale: Helps process emotions and reduce anxiety

interventions.action: Collaborate with physician to assess need for medication adjustment
interventions.rationale: Appropriate pharmacologic control can reduce persistent anxiety

outcomes: Use of at least two effective coping strategies
Improvement in coping score ≥4/10 on coping scale

interventions.action: Identify sources of stress through structured interview
interventions.rationale: Allows focus of coping interventions

interventions.action: Teach step‑by‑step problem‑solving skills
interventions.rationale: Facilitates decision making and reduces sense of helplessness

interventions.action: Encourage participation in support groups or group therapy
interventions.rationale: Increases support network and shares effective strategies

interventions.action: Refer to social worker for community resources and recreational activities
interventions.rationale: Expands coping options beyond the hospital setting

interventions.action: Reinforce daily achievements and record progress in a mood diary
interventions.rationale: Promotes self‑efficacy and motivation

key_points.1.quote: Persistent depressive disorder (also called dysthymia or dysthymic disorder) has less severe depressive symptoms, but they last longer, usually for at least two years.

key_points.3.quote: Most treatments include medicines and/or psychotherapy (talk therapy): Medicines such as antidepressants may help control your symptoms.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Going through trauma or stressful life events may raise your risk even more.

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: Other mental disorders or chronic medical conditions such as diabetes , cancer , or heart disease may occur with depression.

sections.risk_factors.4.quote: For example, the older adult may turn to substances to cope with depression , poor health, injuries, social isolation, a loss of independence, the deaths of spouses and friends, as well as worries about their own mortality.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: To be diagnosed with depression, your symptoms must occur most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Depressants can cause slurred speech, shallow breathing, fatigue, disorientation, lack of coordination, and seizures upon withdrawal from chronic use (Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, 2022).

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: Early symptoms in the disease may include vision changes; insomnia or sleep disturbances; confusion; depression; mood swings; impaired thinking, judgment, and memory; walking and balancing difficulties; and lack of coordination.

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: Patients often experience loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, and their fall risk often increases when they try to go unassisted to the bathroom with these gastrointestinal symptoms.

sections.signs_symptoms.5.quote: Clinical manifestations of dementia include forgetfulness, impaired social skills, and impaired decision-making and thinking abilities that interfere with daily living.

sections.diagnostics.2.quote: A physical exam to make sure another issue isn't causing your symptoms.

sections.complications.1.quote: Behavioral and psychiatric symptoms include poor attention, irritability that can lead to outbursts and aggression, impulsivity, apathy later in the disease, depression, suicidal ideation, psychoses in later stages, lack of awareness, and a lack of insight into the symptoms the individual is experiencing.
